claim: P0 input-completeness closure for the v1p OpenSSH candidate: the analysis identity now binds the data/relocation inputs the derivation reads, and every symbolic residual-bound target carries exactly one disposition.

candidate.note: the run records the working-tree tool digest below; it is not a frozen S commit (AGENTS.md section 22)

analysis_identity.basis: sha256 over, in module-name order, each module name and a canonical JSON input record: every allocated (SHF_ALLOC) section's (name, ELF type, virtual address, size, sha256 of its bytes), the sorted relocation table (section, section-relative offset, type, canonical symbol, addend), the sorted [name, addr, size, kind] defined-symbol rows, the sorted dynamic-symbol rows, and the loader entries (SONAME/NEEDED/RUNPATH/RPATH). Required minimum sections: .text, .plt, .plt.got, .init, .fini, .rodata, .data, .data.rel.ro, .data.rel.ro.local, .got, .got.plt, .init_array, .fini_array; NOBITS sections (address/size only): .bss. Excluded: .debug_*, .zdebug_*, .comment, .note*, .gnu_debuglink, .gnu_debugaltlink, .gnu.build.attributes, every non-allocated section (SHF_ALLOC is absent). ``.llvm.<hash>`` and ``@@VERSION`` suffixes are canonicalised as in the symbol table; the DSO file digest is recorded as a non-identity.

input_enumeration.note: byte ranges and structural facts the DsoGraph derivation reads; the identity binds every allocated (SHF_ALLOC) section, not only the sections the code names explicitly
input_enumeration.all_allocated_note: section_of is unconstrained in cstring_at and switch_targets, so the identity binds every allocated section; the explicit lists below name the sections the derivation reads directly.  The v1p module's actual bound set is the 27 names in analysis_identity.included_sections.

executable_bytes.consumed_by: objdump -d: direct call/jmp edges, address-taken lea/mov comments, indirect-site detection, compiler switch-bound decoding

data_bytes.consumed_by: 8-byte pointer scan (taken_data), static_slot reads, relative jump tables, dlsym string literals, loader roots

nobits.consumed_by: section_of address range; a .bss slot is a zero value

tables: defined-symbol table (nm -S --defined-only): function starts, aliases, sizes, kinds
dynamic-symbol table (nm -D --defined-only): export_index, resolver exports, dynamic-reloc widening
relocation table (readelf -rW): R_X86_64_RELATIVE addends, GLOB_DAT/JUMP_SLOT symbols, R_X86_64_64 symbol+addend
ELF section header table: section names, types, virtual addresses, sizes
excluded: every non-allocated section (SHF_ALLOC is absent), including .symtab/.strtab/.shstrtab and the debug sections

negative.scope: targeted DsoGraph + production build_graph comparison with the precision resolver run on both images; not the full 25-minute closure

positive.note: the closures were not re-run; the old reachable-set evidence in neutral-control.json is retained

comparison_to_v1p_admission.analysis_identity: changed b8f0b873.../v1 -> 3bdf2a60.../v2 because the identity now binds data sections, relocations, the dynamic symbol table and loader entries
comparison_to_v1p_admission.symbol_values: the five symbolic values that v1 counted as unresolved are now dispositioned; all five resolve through the version-stripped export

unbound_inputs: the disassembler/parser binaries (objdump, nm, readelf) are provided by the pinned court image; their versions are an environment input to the derivation and are not hashed into the analysis identity.  The tool digest and court image identity are recorded separately; a toolchain change requires re-measurement.
residuals.note: all five symbolic values and every allocated section are accounted for; the remaining unbound input is the external toolchain, not an ELF input

non_claims: The identity is not a proof of input completeness: it binds the enumerated inputs of the current derivation. A future derivation that starts reading another section must extend the enumeration.
No target was dropped to improve a count. The five symbols are exported by libcrypto; they are resolved through the version-stripped export, not marked external to clear a refusal.
The external-contract table is exact-name and cited; no symbol in this run used it, and it is not a wildcard or a refusal-clearing device.
The reachability algorithm did not change: the reachable-function digest and the edge-record sidecar digest are identical to the v1p admission run.
No obligation is newly discharged: the run remains REFUSED and no SAFE_COMPATIBLE claim is made.
The targeted negative control is not the full closure; it exercises one dispatch slot through the production DsoGraph and build_graph code paths without consumer roots or obligation adjudication.
The run was made from a dirty working tree at 86393abe3; it is not a frozen S commit and its tool digest is the one recorded above.
The analysis identity binds module inputs, not the objdump/nm/readelf toolchain; toolchain identity is recorded separately and a toolchain change requires re-measurement.
